memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Take the following fine spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant calamus, 500 shekels of cassia — all according to the sanctuary shekel — and a hin of olive oil. Make these into a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It will be the sacred anointing oil.'" - Exodus 30:22-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives a precise recipe for the anointing oil — myrrh, cinnamon, calamus, cassia, blended into olive oil by a skilled perfumer. Exact quantities, specific ingredients, expert workmanship. This was not thrown together casually. It was carefully composed to be distinctive and unmistakable.

Interestingly, myrrh appears here at the head of the list. It would appear again at the beginning and end of Jesus' earthly life — brought by the magi to the child (Matt 2:11) and used at His burial (John 19:39). The fragrance associated with anointing accompanied the Anointed One Himself.

Notice too that a blend of different spices made the fragrance. No single ingredient produced it; the beauty came from several combined. That is a picture of God's people as well. Our differences, blended together under God's hand, produce something no individual could achieve alone. Paul says we are to God the pleasing aroma of Christ (2 Cor 2:15). Let God blend your life with others, and let the fragrance rise.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I value how God blends different people together rather than wanting uniformity?
What kind of "fragrance" does my life leave with the people around me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You blend different lives together into something beautiful. Make my life carry the pleasing aroma of Christ, and help me value those You have joined me with. Amen.
